abstract: Challenger, Gray & Christmas's June 2026 layoff report (published July 1, 2026) shows US employers announced 45,849 job cuts in June — down 53% from May's 97,006 — with AI cited as the leading reason for cuts for the fourth consecutive month. AI-attributed layoffs reached 14,029 in June (31% of the monthly total) and 101,743 year-to-date (23% of all cuts). Tech remains the epicenter at 139,156 YTD cuts, up 83% versus first-half 2025.
keyFindings: June 2026 total US layoffs: 45,849 (down 53% from May's 97,006; lowest since December 2025)
AI-attributed layoffs in June 2026: 14,029 (31% of monthly total)
YTD 2026 AI-attributed layoffs: 101,743 (23% of all cuts)
Technology sector YTD 2026 cuts: 139,156 (+83% vs H1 2025)
Tech accounts for nearly one-third of all 2026 layoffs
methodology: Challenger, Gray & Christmas tracks US employer job-cut announcements via press releases, regulatory filings, and direct company statements. AI attribution requires the company to explicitly cite AI/automation/ML as a driver of the cuts. Data covers June 2026 and year-to-date through June 30, 2026.
qualifiers: Challenger is a Tier 3 outplacement-firm data source. AI-attribution is company-declared and may be subject to 'AI washing' (companies citing AI as cover for other cost pressures) — the report itself flags that many 2025 layoffs cited AI without demonstrable AI-related workforce redesign. Also does not distinguish white-collar vs. front-line cuts within each sector, though tech dominance suggests concentration in white-collar/knowledge roles.
